caption:
The 10,000 steps rule has made a lot of people feel like they've failed by 4pm.

A 2025 analysis in The Lancet Public Health pooled 57 studies of about 160,000 adults. Compared with 2,000 steps a day, 7,000 was linked to a 47% lower risk of death and a 38% lower risk of dementia. Going up to 10,000 added little for most outcomes.

Number 1 is my favourite. Three 10-minute walks after meals gets you most of the way there without ever "going for a walk".

What's your daily average right now? Check your phone.

Save this for your next lazy Sunday, and send it to the friend who gives up when they don't hit 10k.
